findings.summary: The rendered canvas is 60.07% fully transparent (605,504 of 1,008,000 pixels at alpha 0), so the figure owns no background: every #111 and #333 label is composited against whatever surface the page supplies, and against a dark surface the title and body text fall to roughly 1.1:1. The card tints at 1.04:1 (#FAFAFA) and 1.06:1 (242,250,245) are invisible on white as well, so the cards are bounded only by their 1.67:1 borders. The same defect was recorded in each earlier figure round of this run and is unchanged.

The two labels that name the transitions are the smallest marks in the figure: "finalize" and "another claim owns the stub" render at 10 px glyph height, about 7 pt on the 1400 px canvas, so at the page's roughly 900 px column they are about 6 px tall. "finalize" also sits 46 px wide in a 77 px gap between two cards, 6 px from the right card's border, so it reads as crowded against the structure it labels.

The two bottom panels carry their content as paragraph prose baked into the picture (100 px of body text each). That text is raster and unselectable in the page, is not searchable, and duplicates what the evidence page's own prose could carry with the page's typography.

The before bars are drawn with alpha=0.45, which renders the draft before-bar as (159,190,208), 1.95:1 against the white canvas, under the 3:1 the style guide asks of a data mark. The largest number in the left panel is the "before 7" bar, and it is the faintest mark in the figure, while the smaller "now 5" bar in the same row is drawn solid.

Both labels of a row are placed at rowmax + 0.25, so a row's "now" label does not sit at its own bar's end: in the draft row the "now 5" label starts at x 516 while its bar ends at x 409, roughly 107 px of whitespace to its left, and it pairs with "before 7" only by vertical offset. A reader scanning left to right can attach the number to the wrong bar.

The right panel's x-axis label is three lines of annotation prose, and its third line ("creation datable on 624 of 10,067") ends at x 1392 of a 1400 px canvas, 7 px of margin from the edge. Nothing is clipped, but the figure carries no right margin and the widest line of a label is what sets the bound.

item_verdicts.contrast: defect in both, non-blocking — image-0's canvas is 60.07% fully transparent, so its text contrast is only true against a white page; image-1's before bars render at 1.95:1, under the 3:1 asked of a data mark. No text falls below AA in either figure.
item_verdicts.data_ink: pass for both — neither carries a grid, key, gradient or decorative fill; every mark either encodes a value or names a state.
item_verdicts.decoration: pass for both — a #FAFAFA card tint and 1 px neutral strokes in image-0, an opaque white canvas with reduced spines in image-1; no gradient, shadow or styled theme anywhere.
item_verdicts.label_collision: pass for both — nothing is clipped at any canvas edge in either figure, no label overlaps another label, and no label is drawn over a bar (verified against all ten measured bar rectangles in image-1).
item_verdicts.legibility: pass for both figures — image-1 reads at a glance at every size; image-0 reads at its native 1400 px, with its two transition labels at 10 px glyph height the weakest marks in either figure.
item_verdicts.table_form: pass for both — a state diagram and a pair of status-count bar charts; neither depicts a row-and-column comparison a table would carry better.

method: Read only. Both attachments were opened with this review node's own Read tool and judged from their pixels, measured with Pillow loading nothing but those two PNGs. No SVG, and no image other than the two named attachments, was opened, read, listed, searched, list-rendered, git-shown or otherwise inspected; the drawing script docs/figures/sn-integrity-backlog/sib-compose-stranded-stubs/sourceless-roster-and-graph.py was read at the reviewed head 3dd0359a only to anchor findings to its lines, and no line of generated markup was used for any verdict. Contrast figures are WCAG ratios computed from the rendered RGB values (relative luminance, sRGB transfer) against the white the figure renders on. Collision verdicts come from measuring the ink: no non-white pixel touches any border of either canvas, and for image-1 each of the ten bar rectangles was measured by contiguous run length and then tested for dark text pixels inside it, of which there were none. Attribution was settled by content plus hash: image-0 is byte-identical (md5 380a15b0eb75ed439d9a14d2852a35a7) to the attachment of the three earlier figure rounds and depicts the sibling run's adoption diagram, and image-1 is the figure the reviewed commit regenerates (81,006 pixels changed against the c29addfc3 render). No figure, script, caption, page or plan was edited, moved, deleted, redrawn, relabelled or reformatted.
notes: No finding blocks. Nothing is clipped in either figure, no label overlaps another label, and no label is drawn over a bar. Two things the previous round recorded as defects in this run's figure are resolved at this head and verified in the render rather than in the script: the "before 0" label no longer sits above a neighbouring bar and the "now 5" label no longer crosses into the before bar, because no dark text pixel falls inside any of the ten measured bar rectangles. The remaining defects in image-1 are matters of emphasis and margin (a faint before bar, a detached label, a 7 px right margin), not of encoding. Image-0 is not this run's figure: it is attached but byte-identical to earlier rounds and belongs to the sibling adoption run, so its three findings are carried forward unchanged rather than newly found.
